newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 11.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 11.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

HAMBURG - Germany's central advertising association (ZAW) criticises the European Commission for failing to provide clear policy on comparative advertising. The ZAW criticises as unclear new directives the commission plans for the European Union regarding comparative, advertising, in which companies compare their products or services to those of competitors. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Liquor manufacturer Weltmarken Import Spirtuosen und Weine GmbH awards its public relations account to the Kohtes & Klewes agency, the agency says. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Frankfurt-based ad agency Boebel/Adam wins a seven-figure account of Carglass Deutschland, a windshield repair company. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
BERLIN - Scientific text publisher Springer posts strong growth in business abroad with foreign turnover climbing 6.5 percent to 561 million marks ($328 million). (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Newspaper readers expect serious content and clear layout, according to a study by the business daily "Handelsblatt" and the association of German newspaper publishers (BDZV). The assumption that younger readers are only interested in short texts and jazzy page designs is false, the Handelsblatt concludes. (Reuter)

COLOGNE - Retail group Metro plans to offer a business television channel and with it, capture a larger communications market segment. Metro unit Satway GmbH&Co KG will manage the channel's development, introduction and sales, says Satway chief exeuctive Axel Werner, as it did for Kaufhof station K-TV.
(Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

WOLFSBURG - Carmaker Volkswagen AG says its group vehicle sales for the the first five months of 1997 rose 9.2 percent to 1.8 million units. VW, the largest carmaker in Europe, also says group car deliveries rose 6.8 percent to 1.1 million units in the period from January to May. VW sells vehicles under the VW, SEAT, Skoda and Audi brand names. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Michael Dell, chief executive of Dell Computer Corp, says he expects the Internet to help increase the company's European sales two to three times faster than the rest of industry over the next few years. "We are quite excited about the outlook for the industry," he says. "We still have very strong targets to grow this (European) business at rates faster than the industry." (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Germans are drinking less liquor and distillers say fewer exports led to a 300 million mark drop in turnover in 1996, says the association of German spirits industry (BSI).
(Reuter)

RUESSELSHEIM - Adam Opel AG, the German unit of U.S. carmaker General Motors Corp says that Juergen Stockmar, Opel board member in charge of the Technical Development Centre is to leave the company. Opel says it agreed to his request to leave the company at a supervisory board meeting. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - Thomas Hille has taken over as marketing and sales chairman of Leica Camera AG in Solms. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Harald Wachenfeld has been named general manager of toy manufacturer Lego's German unit, effective July 1. (Kress)

WALLDORF - The management team of new European online search service Lycos-Bertelsmann is complete. Next to general manager Christopph Mohn, Tony Phillip will service as director of business development. Lycos Deutschland has named Marcus Riecke as its new general manager. His predecessor Stan Sugarmann has joined Gruner + Jahr in its new media division. (Kress)
